body:
Ciaránach is a sacred mountain city within Fein Uaill, distinct from Zarathis and reached from it by a steep pilgrimage road. The pilgrimage reaches its streets, garden and inner citadel through an approach governed by permission, endurance and ritual.

27 September 2025 · the holy road

The recovered pilgrimage begins at Zarathis, follows the river valley through orchards, and climbs into cold, largely untouched mountains. High Lord Bowene calls it a road for the deserving; Captain Haelith describes the journey as a yearly lesson in Zarathian identity. Access is therefore cultural and permission-bound rather than ordinary civic travel.

After a night on the mountain and a further hour of walking, the travelers see a white-and-gold city above the cloud line: ivory-bright walls, silver spires, immaculate streets, and architecture presented as untouched by age or storm. Elenia, Olokun, Scribonia, and Eugene enter with Haelith. Their reactions establish the city’s effect on visitors without proving the narrator’s poetic language to be literal immunity from time.

The Golden Ones

The Golden Ones identify themselves as Ciaránach’s nameless keepers of truth and speak directly into visitors’ minds. Haelith calls them priests devoted to preserving “The Truth” and reports a rumor that they are Verdant Circle mages who discovered immortality. The Codex preserves the first description as their claim and the immortality account as rumor, not settled fact.

Visitors are asked to open their minds and accept the burden of knowledge. Its custodians control access to the archive, testing whether outsiders may receive the knowledge it holds.

The temple in Ciaránach

The temple is preserved as a distinct visual record within the city. The pilgrimage separately identifies Eshnunna as the inner citadel. The supplied temple video is not independently identified as that sanctuary; its dedication, rites and exact place within the city remain unrecovered.

Why the city is sacred

The public record preserves Ciaránach’s sacred importance without disclosing the ancient divine event that gave the city that weight.

December 2025 · counsel becomes law

After Elenia’s confrontation with Magnus, Bowene withdraws to Ciaránach and consults the Golden Ones. On 22 December he descends alone to deliver a compromise: Elenia must leave Fein Uaill, but the door will not be closed forever. Olokun and Aravil stand with her; Adelia and Magnus support exile. Bowene gives Elenia a sending stone, promises continued dialogue, and arranges departure through the Shining Shores toward Babel-Ashur.

Ciaránach’s counsel can shape present law as well as preserve the past. Bowene reports that the Golden Ones agree Zarathian customs may need to change, while insisting that change must be chosen by the people rather than imposed from outside.

The open record

The city’s founding, population, districts, formal government, temple dedication, the Golden Ones’ actual nature, and the limits of their authority remain unresolved. Their claims, Haelith’s report, Bowene’s use of their counsel, and the city’s observed appearance remain separate kinds of evidence.

Separation as part of the city

Ciaránach’s distance from Zarathis is not empty travel time. The road rises from cultivated land into cold, largely untouched mountains, turning physical ascent into preparation. Tradition says the stones remember ancestors who carried civilization into the heights. Whether that language is literal, ceremonial, or both remains unresolved, but it shows how residents understand the journey: reaching the city is itself participation in inherited memory.

The city’s pale gold and white architecture, high spires, processions, and restricted gates express the same principle. The proud and merely curious are said to be turned away, while accepted travelers join a movement already governed by ritual. Outsiders approach its knowledge through the city’s gates, custodians and rules, with no permission to search freely.

Contact without conquest

The admitted party’s greatest established effect was on understanding, not on buildings or government. Their questions, skepticism, reverence, and later dependence on the Golden Ones’ counsel created contact between traditions that had defined themselves through separation. The archive does not yet show the city remade by that encounter, and it should not pretend otherwise.

What changed is the campaign’s relationship to Ciaránach. A remote sacred name became a place player characters had climbed toward, entered, and carried away in memory. Its counsel later shaped Elenia’s exile, proving that guarded history can still exercise direct political force beyond the mountain.

A living sanctuary

Ciaránach remains a functioning holy city rather than an exhausted quest site. Its deepest traditions, the Eternal Flame, the Golden Ones’ knowledge, internal disagreements, and the balance between religious custom and practical protection remain only partly available to outsiders. Those subjects stay unresolved—or protected—until the campaign establishes more.

The city and the sanctuary

The pilgrimage continues through Ciaránach’s streets and upward to a citadel. The narrator names it Eshnunna of the Eternal Flame and describes a further threshold. Ciaránach is the holy city; Eshnunna is the inner sanctuary reached within that journey. Neither is another name for the civic capital of Zarathis.

This distinction describes the approach and the relationship between places. It does not identify every temple in the city with Eshnunna or make the Golden Ones’ understanding of the past infallible. The sanctuary’s restricted revelations remain within the existing protected record.

The night before the final climb

Before that final ascent, Haelith stops the company in the snow and tells them to prepare their minds and shoulders for what they are about to carry. He describes this journey as a lesson taken by people who have earned their community’s trust. The company travels among other pilgrims, rather than finding an empty road waiting only for them.

Eugene fits quietly into the procession; Scribonia tries to follow his example. Once they stop, Haelith sits cross-legged in the fresh snow and watches the meteors. Shelter is permitted, but staying through the cold has a social weight as well as a physical cost. Wind hides the sky for part of the night, and both wizards tire. The narrator distinguishes that exhaustion from a loss of the pilgrims’ respect.

At dawn, Haelith shakes the snow from his wings and leads them onward. Only after another hour do they see the city above the clouds. The preserved date identifies the quest’s opening; the night and following morning belong to the story’s sequence, not to a claim that the whole approach took one hour.

The figures in the garden move

At the entrance, the company does not find an ordinary gate. A transient, golden barrier lies before the city, and the wind sounds through streets quiet of voices. Haelith motions them inside and brings them into a garden. The visitors see what look like tall golden statues, then watch those figures move.

One comes forward, and the welcome sounds in the visitors’ minds. The Golden Ones ask whether they will open their minds and follow. Their account of being nameless and joined to the city remains their own explanation. When one visitor asks to keep his mind private, the keeper allows it.

The procession continues through the city and climbs again to Eshnunna. City, garden and citadel are stages of the approach. The supplied moving image of a temple remains a separate visual record; it has not been independently matched to every threshold described in this quest.

A visit does not make the city freely accessible

When later questions arise, Haelith offers to ask the Golden Ones for answers and warns that their replies can be confusing. Magnus considers visiting them himself. The narrator then makes the access limit explicit: he has not yet earned that permission, while Olokun is closer. Haelith, by contrast, resides there.

The exchange gives the sacred road a continuing place in the region’s life. Someone with access can carry a question, but another person’s curiosity or acquaintance with the captain is not itself admission. The city remains connected to wider affairs through people who can enter and return.

A funeral outside the gates

Aria’s funeral brings the company toward Ciaránach again, by a different road of obligation. After the confrontation at their castle, the mourners walk into Zarathis, then continue with the preserved casket toward Seraphis. The narrator places the Tomb of Heroes high there, just outside Ciaránach’s gates.

The distinction preserves the city’s boundary. Aria is laid to rest in the tomb beyond it; the burial is not placed inside Eshnunna or in every temple shown in the city’s visual records. Read the procession, farewells and burial at Aria’s Tomb →
